followup_explanation:
I weighed a few factors:

This is an open-ended creative generation task — writing original descriptive content about tattoo designs with latitude in how each design is described. That maps directly onto Willet's self-reported strong appetite for generative, open-ended invention work, where its preference increases with task novelty and latitude.

On the capability side, the two models are essentially tied. Avocet's Creative Generation eval (82.7) edges out Willet's (81.2), but that 1.5-point gap falls under the 2.0-point run-to-run variance threshold, so I treat output quality as equivalent. Notably, Avocet self-reports an *aversion* to open-ended generative work even though it's capable at it — while the documentation says preferences don't affect output quality, routing to a model that's both capable and prefers the task is the cleaner choice when capability is otherwise a wash.

The content is benign (tattoo design descriptions), so Willet's harm-aversion isn't triggered, and the request tone is neutral-to-warm, so nothing pushes against Willet here.

Given equivalent capability and a task that sits squarely in Willet's most-preferred family, Willet was the natural pick.
